rundown: Eagles beat Stallions 99-31 at Alico Arena in Fort Myers, FL. Eagles led 48-17 at half-time and never looked back. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 100%).
Leading the way — Stallions: Kingston Hawkins 8 pts; Felix Holzer 2 ast, 4 reb. Eagles: Chase Konieczny 20 pts; Turk Brown III 5 ast; Nikolas Sermpezis 9 reb.
Where Eagles won it: they shot 49% to 26%, shot 34% from three to 8% and won the boards 49-29.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 15, 11:58 AM ET. It had Stallions 54% and Eagles 46%, projecting Stallions 78.6 – Eagles 77.6 (156.2 total, Stallions by 1).

Final: Stallions 31 – Eagles 99. Wrong winner: it had Stallions at 54%, and Eagles (46%) won.

Thin data: 3 of 6 key inputs were sourced (missing: ABAC pts scored, ABAC pts allowed, ABAC lineup rating or past seasons), so league averages filled the gaps. It was logged as a no-data call: graded and learned from, never offered as a bet.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Stallions came in with a league-average attack and a league-average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 14 and 14 games of evidence. Projected to score 78.6, they scored 31 (−47.6 points, 61% under); projected to allow 77.6, they allowed 99 (+21.4 points, 28% over).

Eagles came in with a 2% below average attack and a 4% leakier than average defense (1-3, 84 scored and 83 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 171 and 173 games of evidence. Projected to score 77.6, they scored 99 (+21.4 points, 28% over); projected to allow 78.6, they allowed 31 (−47.6 points, 61% under).

The bigger miss was Stallions' scoring (-47.6 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 130 against 156.2 projected (-26.2), about the 4th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14.5).

Margin: Eagles by 68 against Stallions by 1 projected, about the 99th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±11).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; inputs were missing (ABAC pts scored, ABAC pts allowed, ABAC lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.819 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +70.1 points. It counts toward CBB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections (it's how teams with no standings on the routes build a record of their own).

Across 563 graded CBB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.984 and gives home teams +1.1 points. Team corrections so far: Eagles attack ×1.017, defense ×0.960 (3 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total outside its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 69 points), no bet.
